text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- All parliamentary parties signed a statement declaring support for Slovenia's bid to join NATO as soon as possible.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday told his Slovenian counterpart Zoran Thaler he strongly supported Slovenia's bids to join the European Union and NATO.
- Employees of Slovenian Railways said they would go on strike for an hour on April 22 to demand higher salaries.
- The controlling board of the city of Trzic said the mayor Pavel Rupar breached his authority when granting finances for various projects.
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan visited Norway on Thursday and met King Harald V.
- The government passed a draft law on ratification of the association agreement with the European Union, which is expected to be adopted by parliament in May.

- Publisher Mladinska Knjiga Zalozba has not yet completed its privatisation process because of legal problems following the 1996 Payment Agency decision that the company has to reverse its 1991 partial privatisation scheme due to irregularities.
